title: Model-tier SLI inheritance and regional failover playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: define a practical SLI/SLO inheritance model for model endpoints and model variants, codify error-budget driven adaptive circuit-breaker thresholds, and publish a regional failover + load-shedding playbook. This ticket produces an operational policy and runbook for platform teams and on-call to ensure graceful degradation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI set is defined for model endpoints and for model variants (e.g., base model vs. quantized variant) with explicit aggregation rules.
An error budget policy with burn-rate bands and automated actions is documented and wired into alerting (pager + slack channels) for production clusters.
Circuit breaker thresholds (latency, error rate, concurrency) are defined per traffic tier and per model size with concrete default values and rationales.
A multi-region failover decision tree and traffic shift recipe (warm standby, progressive cutover percentages) is captured and linked to routing automation playbooks.
Load-shedding strategies prioritized by UX impact (e.g., degrade to streaming-only tokens, switch to smaller model, deny non-critical routes) are enumerated with rollout recipes.
Runbook includes links to dashboards, queries, and a sample incident timeline for a simulated cross-region outage.
Design doc and RFC have at least two engineering reviews and a PM sign-off; PRs linked and ready for merge.
Tests: a chaos test that simulates 50% region capacity loss and verifies automated failover and no user-visible errors above defined SLO breach window.
description_long: Background: We've historically measured availability at a fleet level. As customers pin endpoints to specific model versions and variants (float16, int8, pipeline-quant), we need clearer per-entity SLIs and a policy that scales across wild-card endpoints. This doc proposes: 1) SLI inheritance: endpoint -> model family -> variant, with weighted aggregation for SLO burn accounting; 2) Error-budget bands: Normal/Watch/Critical and automated runbook actions including throttling and variant fallback; 3) Circuit breakers that use dynamic thresholds derived from recent p95/p99 latency baselines and token-concurrency percentiles; 4) Multi-region failover recipe: warm-standby provisioning, DNS and LB steps, sample traffic-shift percentages, and safety checks; 5) Load-shedding strategies ordered by least-customer-impact-first and how to implement them safely (graceful stream truncation, model swap, queued requests with max-wait).
comments: 2025-01-10 Maya Chen: Drafted the SLI inheritance rules. Key point: model-variant should inherit the endpoint SLO but carry its own micro-SLI for quantization errors and generation truncations.
2025-01-15 Liam O'Connor: Reviewed draft. Added proposal for weighted error budgeting: allocate 70% of endpoint error budget to primary variant, 30% to fallback variants to avoid silent overuse.

2025-01-22 Priya Nair (SRE): Suggested we derive circuit-breaker concurrency thresholds from 95th percentile token throughput per GPU type; this will allow sane defaults across Dedicated and Hosted clusters.

2025-01-29 Engineering sync: Agreed on three burn-rate bands: green (burn <= 1x), amber (1x < burn <= 4x) with throttling, red (burn > 4x) triggers automated failover and aggressive shedding. Action owners assigned.

2025-02-03 Ethan Ruiz (PM): Added customer-impact taxonomy and gate: any plan that moves customer traffic across regions requires SOC/Legal pre-approval for Private deployments. Marked in dependencies.
2025-02-08 QA: Added chaos test plan to simulate region outage and measure time-to-recover and SLO breach windows. Test ticket created ENG-31809.
2025-02-11 Liam O'Connor: Uploaded sample Grafana queries and alert rules to runbook. Requesting one more engineering review before merging RFC.

2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Incorporated feedback on fallback ordering; changed default fallback sequence to (1) smaller model variant, (2) quantized variant, (3) reduced-context mode, (4) deny non-critical routes. Moving to In Review.
implementation_notes: Default SLIs to track per endpoint: success_rate (200-series responses with non-empty generation), p99 end-to-end latency (ingress->final_token), interleaved_error_rate (invalid model responses), and quality_regressions (eval set passthrough failures).
Variant-specific SLIs: token-truncation-rate, quantization-artifact-rate (detected by eval proxies), and peak-GPU-utilization fractional SLI for Dedicated pools.

Circuit-breakers: maintain moving-window baselines (30m) and calculate thresholds at baseline * factor (factor=2.5 for p95 latency, factor=4 for p99). When threshold hit and burn-rate in amber, start progressive throttling; in red, start traffic shift to warm-standby region.

Failover recipe: precondition checks (region health >= 70%, capacity pre-warmed, KMS keys available in target region), then progressive traffic shift sequence: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 5–10 minute observation windows and rollback on error-rate delta > 2x baseline.

Load-shedding order: (A) prefer model-quality-preserving measures (reduce batch size, increase batching window), (B) swap to smaller model family with identical instruction alignment, (C) graceful streaming truncation with rationale header, (D) deny or queue low-priority admin routes.
Monitoring: add alerts for combined signals (error-rate > threshold AND burn-rate > band) to reduce false positives. Pager on red-band incidents only.
Backstop: maintain a global circuit-breaker that can be manually toggled by SRE in extreme circumstances to cut non-critical tenants.
